question: Fiery Indian curries and spicy Thai dishes had no chili peppers at all until about 500 years ago. From which part of the world did chilies first arrive?
topic: Spices and herbs and where they came from
source_excerpt: The rapid introduction of chilies to Africa and Asia was likely through Portuguese and Spanish traders in the 16th century

extra.why_interesting: Players assume chili heat is ancient and native to Indian and Thai cooking. In fact those cuisines had no chilies until about 500 years ago. The stem gives enough to reason it out: 'arrived 500 years ago' points to Columbus and the New World.
extra.verification_notes: Chilies originated in the Americas and reached Asia via Portuguese/Spanish traders in the 16th century, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chili_pepper

explanation: Chilies are native to the Americas, and Portuguese and Spanish traders carried them to Asia after Columbus. Before that, Indian cooks got their heat from black pepper and long pepper.

question: Black, white and green peppercorns sit side by side on supermarket shelves. How many different kinds of plant do they come from?
topic: Spices and herbs and where they came from
source_excerpt: Green pepper, like black pepper, is made from unripe drupes.

extra.why_interesting: Almost everyone has seen black, white and green pepper on shelves and assumes they are different plants. The answer, a single vine, gives a satisfying 'huh, really?' moment. Pink peppercorns are left out because they come from an unrelated tree.
extra.verification_notes: Black, white and green peppercorns are all Piper nigrum, processed or harvested differently (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pepper).

explanation: All three grow on the same pepper vine. Green ones are picked unripe, black ones are picked unripe and then dried until they darken, and white ones are ripe berries with their skin soaked off.
